name: Welcome Back, Kotter
s: Gabe Kotter returns to his old high school -- this time as a teacher. He's put in charge of a class full of unruly remedial students called the Sweathogs. They're a bunch of wisecracking, underachieving and incorrigible students, and it takes all of Mr. Kotter's humor -- and experience as a former Sweathog himself -- to deal with his class.

paragraphs.text: Welcome Back, Kotter is an American sitcom starring Gabe Kaplan as a high-school teacher in charge of an ethnically diverse remedial education class. Several students in the class have nicknamed themselves the Sweathogs. Recorded in front of a live studio audience, the series aired on ABC from September 9, 1975, through June 8, 1979. It provided John Travolta his breakthrough role.

Stand-up comedian and actor Gabriel "Gabe" Kaplan stars as the main character, Gabe Kotter, a wise-cracking teacher who returns to his alma mater—James Buchanan High School in Bensonhurst, Brooklyn, New York City—10 years after graduating, to teach a remedial class of loafers known as the Sweathogs. The rigid vice principal, Michael Woodman (John Sylvester White), who was formerly Kotter's social studies teacher, dismisses the Sweathogs as witless hoodlums. Woodman only expects Kotter to contain them until they drop out or are expelled or arrested. Kotter had been a remedial student and a founding member of the original class of Sweathogs. The fictional James Buchanan High is based on the Brooklyn high school that Kaplan attended in real life, New Utrecht High School, which is shown in the opening credits. Many of the show's characters were based on people Kaplan knew during his teen years as a remedial student, several of whom were described in one of Kaplan's stand-up comic routines "Holes and Mellow Rolls".

The character Vinnie Barbarino was inspired by Eddie Lecarri and Ray Barbarino, the character Freddie "Boom Boom" Washington was inspired by Freddie "Furdy" Peyton, the character Juan Epstein was partially inspired by Epstein "The Animal", and the character Arnold Horshack was inspired by someone of the same name.
